body: Distillation attacks copy the reasoning capabilities of closed-source large language models, allowing bad actors to replicate state-of-the-art performance at low cost. Attackers systematically collect a large volume of frontier model reasoning traces and then train (i.e., "distill") their own models on these traces. Existing defenses against distillation attacks are typically evaluated immediately after distillation, implicitly assuming attackers do not train their models any further. In this paper, we argue that a more realistic threat model includes further training with reinforcement learning after distillation. A misspecified threat model can give a false sense of security -- some defenses that seem effective after distillation can be broken after subsequent reinforcement learning. Practically, reinforcement learning lowers the bar for a distillation attack to be effective. We show that simple attacks can steal reasoning capabilities from existing closed-source language models using data easily obtainable from current APIs, yielding reasoning improvements equivalent to more sophisticated attacks that extract the full hidden traces. Results indicate that any distillation defense that leaks sufficient information to reconstruct approximate reasoning traces is likely ineffective. We conclude by discussing broader implications and batch-level distillation defenses which could be more effective.
summaryZh: 本文探讨了闭源大语言模型面临的知识蒸馏攻击与防御机制。研究指出，现有的蒸馏防御通常在蒸馏后立即评估，假设攻击者不再进一步训练模型。然而，更为现实的威胁模型包括在蒸馏后通过强化学习进行微调。实验表明，简单的攻击配合后续强化学习即可轻松突破看似有效的防御，使得基于API获取的数据能够窃取推理能力。文章最后讨论了批量蒸馏防御等更具潜力的防范方向。

aiReview.reasonZh: 该研究表明知识蒸馏防御在结合强化学习后容易被攻破，对闭源模型的安全威胁模型提出了重要修正。

glossary.explanationZh: 知识蒸馏，指通过模仿前沿模型的推理痕迹来低成本复制其能力的攻击或训练方法
强化学习，文章指在蒸馏后进一步训练模型以降低攻击门槛的阶段
威胁模型，评估安全机制时对攻击者行为和能力的假设界定
推理痕迹，前沿大模型在解决复杂问题时生成的中间思考过程数据
批处理级蒸馏防御，文中讨论的可能比现有方法更有效的潜在防御策略
